1.6 — Animation States: IsWalking, WalkDir, Attack

Your player moves through space, but it does not look alive yet. Today, you connect code to Unity's Animator state machine: reading parameters, driving directional clips, flipping sprites, and understanding why code sets state while the engine plays frames.

Read the Docs ~15 min

In professional game engines, scripts rarely swap individual sprite images directly. Instead, the visual engine uses an Animator Controller — a visual finite state machine. Your C# script communicates with the Animator by setting parameters:

Engine APISignature / TypeDescription & Behavior
animator.SetBool() void SetBool(string name, bool value) Sets a boolean condition parameter on the Animator Controller. Used for persistent continuous states (e.g. idle vs walking).
animator.SetInteger() void SetInteger(string name, int value) Sets an integer parameter. Used for discrete multi-state selection (e.g. direction: 0 = up, 1 = side, 2 = down).
animator.SetTrigger() void SetTrigger(string name) Fires a momentary trigger parameter that resets automatically once consumed by a transition. Used for one-shot actions like attacks or jumps.
spriteRenderer.flipX bool (read/write) Horizontally mirrors the sprite texture across its vertical axis. Allows a single sideways walk animation to serve for both left and right.
Mathf.Abs() float Mathf.Abs(float f) Returns the absolute value of a number (stripping negative signs). Essential for comparing speed magnitudes regardless of direction.

Socratic: Separation of Concerns

  1. Why does the C# script set abstract parameters like "IsWalking" or "WalkDir" instead of telling the engine "play frame 4 of the walk sprite sheet"?
  2. What would happen to your code if an artist decided to replace a 4-frame walk animation with an 8-frame walk animation? If your code only sets parameters, does any C# have to change?
  3. What is the technical difference between setting a boolean with SetBool versus firing an action with SetTrigger?
Read Function-Level Examples ~15 min

Notice how each visual function and parameter type works in isolation across completely different characters:

Example 1 — Setting a Boolean State on a Scuba Diver:

// Drives a continuous state transition (e.g. idle on boat vs swimming underwater)
animator.SetBool("IsSwimming", waterDepth > 0f);

Example 2 — Setting an Integer Discrete State on a Warrior:

// Selects an equipment stance: 0 = Unarmed, 1 = Sword/Shield, 2 = Greatsword
animator.SetInteger("WeaponStance", 2);

Example 3 — Firing a One-Shot Action Trigger on a Wizard:

// Fires a momentary action clip that plays once and returns to the default state
if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.Space))
{
    animator.SetTrigger("CastSpell");
}

Example 4 — Flipping a 2D Sprite on a Flying Falcon:

// Horizontally mirrors the sprite texture based on whether flight velocity is negative
spriteRenderer.flipX = horizontalVelocity < 0f;

Example 5 — Stripping Negative Signs with Absolute Value:

// Mathf.Abs turns -4.5 into +4.5, making it easy to compare magnitudes regardless of sign
if (Mathf.Abs(steerX) >= Mathf.Abs(steerY))
{
    // Horizontal magnitude is stronger than vertical
}

Predict Before Building

  1. If steerX is -0.8 and steerY is 0.3, what does Mathf.Abs(steerX) >= Mathf.Abs(steerY) evaluate to?
  2. Why is SetTrigger preferred over SetBool for an attack swing or spell cast?
Build Lab: Your Turn ~25 min

Step 1 — Read the Animator Controller in Unity. Select the Player in the Overworld scene, then open Window → Animation → Animator.

  1. Click the Parameters tab in the top-left of the Animator window. Notice the three parameters already configured: IsWalking (Bool), WalkDir (Int), and Attack (Trigger).
  2. Click the transition arrow pointing from the side-walking state to the idle state. In the Inspector, read its condition: IsWalking == false.
  3. Click the arrows between up, side, and down: notice they evaluate WalkDir equals 0 (up), 1 (side), and 2 (down).
Architectural Specification for PlayerController.cs:

Component References:

  • What components control visual sprite display and animation playback on the player?
  • If those components live on child GameObjects, what method finds components located in children?
  • In which lifecycle method should you cache these component references so you only look them up once?

Dedicated Animation Method:

  • Should animation state logic clutter your movement calculations, or be organized in a dedicated helper function?
  • Where must this helper method be called each frame to keep visuals in sync with input?

Sub-Problem 1 (Evaluate Walking State):

  • How can you determine if the player is currently moving in any direction? What condition checks if either horizontal or vertical input is non-zero?
  • What Animator method updates a boolean parameter? What is the exact name of the boolean parameter in the Animator Controller?

Sub-Problem 2 (Evaluate Direction & Flip):

  • When moving diagonally, how do you decide whether the sprite should play the sideways or vertical animation? How does Mathf.Abs() help compare horizontal vs vertical magnitude?
  • If horizontal movement dominates:
    • What integer value corresponds to the side-walking state in the Animator Controller?
    • How do you determine whether sprite.flipX should be true or false based on movement direction?
  • If vertical movement dominates:
    • What integer value corresponds to walking up? What integer corresponds to walking down?
    • Do you need to set sprite.flipX when moving vertically?

Sub-Problem 3 (Attack Trigger):

  • What function detects when the player clicks the left mouse button (mouse button index 0)?
  • What Animator method fires a one-shot trigger parameter? What is the trigger parameter's name?

Save PlayerController.cs and return to Unity. Press Play. Walk in all four directions. Your character should now smoothly transition between idle, walking sideways, walking up, and walking down, with proper left/right sprite flipping!

Bug Hunt: Diagnosing Animation Faults

  1. What happens if you misspell "IsWalking" as "isWalking" (lowercase i) in your C# code? What does the Unity Console report?
  2. Temporarily comment out the line setting sprite.flipX. Which direction can your player never face?
  3. What happens if you click the mouse rapidly? Does the attack animation trigger cleanly and return to walking/idle?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Exploring State Transitions

  1. Open the Animator window while the game is running in Play mode. Walk around. Notice the blue progress bar on each animation state indicating playback time, and observe the transitions highlighting in real time!
  2. The player prefab includes animation clips for holding tools/weapons (e.g. shovel, axe). In the Animator window, find where the alternate weapon states are located. What conditions govern their transitions?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Open the Animator Controller window and inspect states, arrows, and parameter conditions
  • Explain the distinct purposes of SetBool, SetInteger, and SetTrigger
  • Explain the software architecture split: code sets state parameters, the Animator Controller plays visual clips
  • Use Mathf.Abs() to resolve dominant directional input
  • Commit your working animation controller integration to GitHub
